subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Ethical, legal, cultural and environmental impacts
Privacy and open source vs proprietary

questions.q: Which Act makes unauthorised access to computer material a criminal offence?
questions.explain: The Computer Misuse Act 1990 criminalises unauthorised access to and modification of computer material.

questions.q: Which piece of legislation currently governs how organisations store and process personal data in the UK?
questions.explain: The Data Protection Act 2018 controls how personal data is used and enshrines UK data protection principles.

questions.q: Which Act protects the intellectual work of a programmer or author from being copied without permission?
questions.explain: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 protects original works, including software, from unauthorised copying.

questions.q: What is a defining feature of open source software?
options: Its source code is made freely available to view and modify
It can never be sold for money
It contains no bugs because experts write it
It works only on Linux operating systems
questions.explain: Open source software is distributed with its source code so users can study, change and share it.

questions.q: Which statement best describes proprietary software?
options: The source code is kept secret and use is restricted by a licence
The source code is always published online for free
It cannot be updated after purchase
It must be written in a compiled language
questions.explain: Proprietary software keeps its source code closed and controls use through a licence agreement.

questions.q: Which of these is an environmental impact of computing technology?
questions.explain: Discarded devices create e-waste, which can release harmful materials and is an environmental concern.

questions.q: The term 'digital divide' refers to which cultural issue?
options: The gap between those with and without access to technology
The difference between analogue and digital signals
The split between hardware and software costs
questions.explain: The digital divide describes inequality in access to computers and the internet across a population.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the offences defined by the Computer Misuse Act 1990?
questions.explain: Unauthorised access to computer material (basic hacking) is the first offence under the Act.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an ethical (rather than legal) issue in computing?
options: Whether it is fair for AI to replace human workers
Copying software in breach of its licence
Keeping personal data longer than allowed
questions.explain: Ethical issues concern what is right or fair, whereas the other options break specific laws.

questions.q: Why might a business prefer proprietary software over open source software?
options: It usually comes with dedicated professional support and warranties
Its source code can always be edited freely
It is guaranteed to be completely free of charge
questions.explain: Proprietary vendors typically provide guaranteed technical support, updates and accountability.

questions.q: Which is a genuine advantage of open source software for a school?
options: It can be adapted to the school's needs and often has no licensing cost
It always outperforms every proprietary alternative
It cannot contain any security vulnerabilities
It is legally exempt from copyright
questions.explain: Open source can be modified freely and is frequently free to use, reducing costs.

questions.q: Under the Data Protection Act 2018, which principle must organisations follow?
options: Personal data must be kept accurate and up to date
Personal data can be shared with anyone who asks
Personal data must be kept forever as a record
Personal data may be used for any new purpose
questions.explain: Keeping data accurate and up to date is one of the core data protection principles.

questions.q: Why are large data centres a concern for the environment?
options: They consume large amounts of electricity for power and cooling
They reduce the number of servers needed worldwide
They remove the need for any electricity
They only ever run on renewable energy
questions.explain: Data centres use significant energy to run and cool servers, raising their carbon footprint.

questions.q: A company collects customer browsing data to target adverts. Which issue does this MOST directly raise?
questions.explain: Collecting and using personal browsing data without clear consent is primarily a privacy concern.

questions.q: Which action would help protect an individual's privacy online?
options: Reviewing and limiting an app's data permissions
Sharing your location publicly on all posts
questions.explain: Restricting the data an app can access reduces how much personal information is collected.

questions.q: Which of these is a cultural impact of the widespread use of automation and robots in industry?
options: Some manual jobs are lost while new technical jobs are created
The Data Protection Act no longer applies
questions.explain: Automation changes the workforce, removing some roles while creating demand for new skills.

questions.q: A student guesses a teacher's password and logs in to read exam files, changing nothing. Which law has been broken?
questions.explain: Gaining unauthorised access to computer material is an offence under the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.q: A person downloads a paid game, then copies and sells it to classmates. Which law has been broken?
questions.explain: Copying and selling software without permission infringes the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988.

questions.q: An attacker writes a virus that deletes files on other people's computers. Which offence under the Computer Misuse Act does this best match?
options: Unauthorised acts with intent to impair the operation of a computer
Fair and lawful processing of data
Keeping data accurate and up to date
questions.explain: Deliberately damaging or modifying data with malware is the third offence under the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.q: An online shop leaves its customer database unencrypted and it is stolen. Which law is the shop most likely to have breached?
options: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974
questions.explain: Failing to keep personal data secure breaches the security principle of the Data Protection Act 2018.
